key_insight: A proposed dense silicon spin-qubit architecture combines surface-code memories, transport lanes, and routing junctions to support scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.
engineering_relevance: The design links qubit storage, connectivity, logical gates, and CMOS-compatible multiplexed wiring in a semiconductor integration roadmap.
method: Store rotated surface-code logical qubits in memories supporting logical single-qubit operations.
Connect memories through one-dimensional spin-shuttling lanes and cross junctions implementing transversal logical CNOT gates.
Evaluate logical error rates and wiring constraints using experimentally demonstrated silicon spin-qubit parameters.
evidence_signal: The analysis estimates that code distance ≥21 is needed for logical error rates below 10⁻¹⁰ per syndrome cycle and that optimized wiring could enable over 120,000 logical qubits on a 100 mm × 100 mm chip.
watch_item: These are architectural estimates rather than a demonstrated integrated system; scaling depends on reliable shuttling, junction operations, and optimized wiring.
paper_title: A scalable dense silicon qubit architecture with logical operations
